prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-05-05. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.53 |
| Retained earnings       | 15,795M |
| Current liabilities     | 12,594M |
| Current assets          | 6,623M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 31,808M |
| Total liabilities       | 84,798M |
| Total assets            | 117,776M |
| EBIT / operating income | 1,360M |
| Revenue                 | 6,020M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-05-05, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported current ratio of 0.53 signals acute liquidity pressure and an inability to cover near-term obligations from liquid assets. Combined with high leverage (total liabilities ~72% of assets) this points to an elevated risk of financial stress, even though positive retained earnings, equity, and EBIT provide some offset and rule out near-term default or CCC-range distress.
DECISION: BB-
(The rating reflects only the static ratios given and pre-2026 norms for non-financial issuers; interest coverage and cash-flow data are absent, limiting granularity.)
